_comment: The public small-machine workload. Binds the published salt-shaker fixture by contract (node-salt-shaker-js@1.0): clone github.com/kstrat2001/salt-shaker, `darkmux lab fixture register <path>`, then `darkmux lab run salt-shaker -p <profile>`. No tools: the numbered source is in the prompt, the reply's FIX lines are applied by the reply-patch provider, and `npm test` judges the result. Sized for an 8 GB machine: about 2,000 prompt tokens, a two-line reply.

workload.description: Two named bugs in a 44-line duration parser on the public salt-shaker fixture (github.com/kstrat2001/salt-shaker, MIT). The model reads the numbered file with no tools and replies with the two corrected lines; the harness applies them and runs the suite (baseline 6 passing, 3 failing). Measured on 2026-10-22: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 fixes both on an 8 GB M2; Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B fix neither.
workload.prompt:
Below is src/duration.js, shown with line numbers. Its function `parseDuration(text)` turns strings like "1h30m" into milliseconds. It has exactly two bugs:

- Line 15 has the wrong multiplier for minutes.
- Line 40 rejects exactly seven days, which should be allowed.

```js
${PATCH_FILE}
```

Reply with exactly two lines and nothing else:

FIX 15: <the corrected line 15>
FIX 40: <the corrected line 40>
